root_causes.description: product-catalog, a leaf service with no downstream dependencies, exhibited a severe p99 latency spike (~9600ms, max 10000ms) with zero errors, normal CPU (0.011 cores), normal memory (~23.7MB), and no pod restarts. This is a pure latency fault in product-catalog that propagated to all of its callers.

evidence.observed_value: p99_latency_ms mean=2007.572, p95=8001.918, p99=9600.384, max=10000.000 during incident window

evidence.expected_baseline: error_rate < 0.01 — confirms latency-only fault, not http_abort

evidence.observed_value: memory_usage mean=23760896 bytes, max=23904256 bytes (no anomaly)

evidence.query_or_id: search_traces service_name=product-catalog min_duration_ms=5000: 16 total, 0 errors, p95_duration=39924ms; trace 2b40c40b443d1ce0 (user_checkout_single, 16246ms, ok), e5a6d0ab1f739b20 (user_browse_product, 5403ms, ok), 316c20fabcc43e85 (user_get_recommendations, 16133ms, ok)
evidence.observed_value: 16 slow traces, 0 errors, p95 duration 39924ms — all successful but extremely slow
no logs found — no application errors during incident
evidence.expected_baseline: no error logs — consistent with latency-only fault

root_causes.description: checkout's p99 latency spiked to ~9409ms because it synchronously calls product-catalog (per topology: checkout → cart, payment, email, shipping, currency, product-catalog). Its other leaf dependencies (payment 1.98ms, cart 3.88ms, shipping 1.98ms) were healthy, confirming the latency is inherited from product-catalog.

evidence.observed_value: payment p99=1.980ms, no anomaly — checkout's other dependencies healthy

root_causes.description: frontend (the user-facing entry point, called by load-generator) showed p99 ~9601ms, matching the watchdog alert. Per topology, frontend calls product-catalog directly and via checkout/recommendation, so its latency is fully explained by downstream propagation from the product-catalog latency fault.

evidence.observed_value: recommendation p99=4627.399ms (elevated; calls product-catalog per topology)

remediation_steps: Inspect product-catalog for the source of the ~10s delay: check flagd feature flag configuration for any latency-experiment flag enabled on product-catalog, and review recent deployments/config changes to the product-catalog deployment in otel-demo namespace.
Restart or roll back the product-catalog deployment (kubectl -n otel-demo rollout restart deployment/product-catalog) to clear the injected delay if it is process-local.
Add aggressive timeouts and circuit breakers in frontend/checkout/recommendation for product-catalog calls so a single slow dependency cannot inflate end-user p99 to 10s.
Verify recovery by re-checking p99 latency for product-catalog, checkout, and frontend after remediation; confirm error rates remain at 0.
Add a latency SLO/alert on product-catalog (leaf service) so future latency faults are caught at the origin rather than at the frontend.
